acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause define the main terms the agreement relies on (for example services or deliverables, confidential information, fees)? (2) Does each definition identify what it covers with clear boundaries? (3) Is any term defined more than once with different meanings within the clause? (4) Does the clause state rules for reading the agreement (for example headings do not affect meaning, singular includes plural, references to laws include amendments)? (5) [Only where a definition relies on another document, law or standard] Where a definition relies on another document, law or standard, is the source identified specifically (by name, and by version or date where the source changes over time)? (6) [Balance] [Only where a definition extends to affiliates, group companies or related entities] Is the extension to affiliates or related entities limited by a stated test (for example ownership or control)? (7) Do the definitions only describe terms, without creating obligations, rights, exclusions or limits?
unacceptable_triggers: Main terms are defined: No main terms are defined (DEF-01)
Definitions are precise: Most definitions are open-ended or circular (DEF-02)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause state what the agreement is for (the services or relationship it covers)? (2) Does the clause describe the purpose in the same way throughout, without conflicting statements? (3) Does the clause avoid creating obligations, rights or restrictions?

The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause identify the services to be provided (by description, list or reference to a schedule)? (2) Does the clause say what is outside the scope of the services? (3) [Balance] [Only where the clause lets the scope expand or change] Is the growth or change of scope limited by agreement or a change process? (4) Does the clause identify who receives or may use the services (for example the customer and named affiliates)? (5) Does the clause say where detailed service requirements are set (for example a SoW or schedule)?
unacceptable_triggers: Services are identified: The services are not identified (SCO-01)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause say what each statement of work or work order must contain (for example scope, deliverables, timeline, fees)? (2) Does the clause say how a statement of work is agreed and becomes binding? (3) Does the clause set a process for changing a statement of work (for example request, assessment, written approval)? (4) [Balance] Can a statement of work be changed or issued only with the agreement of both parties? (5) Does the clause say how a statement of work relates to the master agreement and what applies if they conflict? (6) Does the clause say whether one statement of work can end without ending the master agreement or other work orders? (7) Does the clause require each statement of work to state how the work is priced (for example fixed price, time and materials)?
unacceptable_triggers: SoW content is required: No content requirements are stated (SOW-01)
How a SoW becomes binding: No mechanism is stated (SOW-02)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Are the customer's obligations described specifically (for example access, information, approvals, resources) rather than only as 'cooperation'? (2) Does the clause say when the customer must act (for example when to give information or approvals)? (3) Does the clause state what follows if the customer does not perform an obligation? (4) [Balance] [Only where the clause states a consequence for customer non-performance] Is the consequence limited to a defined remedy (for example time or cost relief) rather than open-ended liability or termination? (5) [Balance] [Only where the clause lets a party claim relief for customer delay] Is that relief conditional on prompt written notice of the problem? (6) [Balance] [Only where the clause lets a party claim relief for customer delay] Must the party claiming relief take reasonable steps to limit the impact of the delay?
unacceptable_triggers: Obligations are specific: Only broad 'cooperation' wording is used (CUS-01)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause state what the provider must do (identified duties, not just 'provide the services')? (2) Does the clause set a standard for how the provider performs (a named standard, specification or defined test)? (3) Does the clause state when the provider's obligations must be performed? (4) Does the clause say what follows if the provider does not perform (for example re-performance, credit, termination)? (5) [Only where the clause deals with the provider's personnel] Does the clause require personnel to be suitably qualified or skilled? (6) [Only where the clause identifies key personnel] Is replacement of key personnel subject to notice or consent? (7) [Balance] [Only where the clause deals with the provider's personnel] Can a party require removal or replacement of personnel on stated grounds? (8) [Only where the clause deals with the provider's personnel] Does the clause state which party is responsible for personnel's pay, taxes and benefits? (9) [Only where the clause deals with the provider's personnel] Are personnel required to follow the other party's policies or rules, and are those identified or provided? (10) [Balance] [Only where the clause restricts hiring or soliciting personnel] Is the restriction mutual, limited in time and limited in scope?
unacceptable_triggers: Obligations are specific: No duties are stated (SPO-01)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause state the grounds on which a party may terminate (for example material breach, insolvency)? (2) [Balance] Are termination rights available to both parties, or, if one-sided, is the difference limited? (3) [Only where the clause allows termination for breach] Is a chance to remedy the breach stated with a definite period? (4) [Only where the clause allows termination without cause (for convenience)] Is a notice period stated for termination without cause? (5) Does the clause require termination by written notice and say when termination takes effect? (6) [Balance] [Only where the clause allows suspension of services] Does the clause limit suspension by grounds, prior notice and restoration of service? (7) Does the clause say what happens on termination (for example payment for work done, refund of prepaid amounts, return of materials)? (8) Does the clause say which provisions continue after termination? (9) Does the clause refer to exit or transition arrangements? (10) [Only where the clause deals with exit, transition or handover] Does the clause require assistance on exit or transition? (11) [Only where the clause deals with exit, transition or handover] Does the clause say what assistance includes (for example data return, handover, knowledge transfer, continued service)? (12) [Only where the clause deals with exit, transition or handover] Is the period of assistance stated? (13) [Only where the clause deals with exit, transition or handover] Does the clause require an exit or transition plan? (14) [Only where the clause deals with exit, transition or handover] Does the clause say on what terms (for example fees, standards) services continue during exit? (15) [Only where the clause covers return of data] Does the clause say when and in what format data is returned? (16) [Only where the clause deals with exit, transition or handover] Does the clause say whether and how assistance is charged? (17) [Only where the clause deals with exit, transition or handover] Must the party cooperate with any replacement provider?
unacceptable_triggers: Grounds for termination: No ground is stated (TER-01)
Notice for termination without cause: No notice period is stated (TER-04)
Assistance is required: It is not required (TER-10)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Are the deliverables identified by description or specification? (2) Does the clause give delivery dates or a definite way to work them out? (3) Does the clause state the criteria or tests used to accept a deliverable? (4) Is the period for reviewing a deliverable stated? (5) Does the clause say what happens if the reviewing party does not respond within the review period? (6) [Balance] [Only where the clause treats silence or non-response as acceptance] Is acceptance by silence conditional on a reminder or further notice? (7) Does the clause say what happens when a deliverable is rejected (reasons, correction, re-submission)? (8) Does the clause state a consequence if deliverables repeatedly fail acceptance (for example termination or refund)? (9) [Balance] Does the clause say whether acceptance affects the right to raise defects found later?
unacceptable_triggers: Deliverables are identified: Deliverables are not identified (DEL-01)
Acceptance criteria: No criteria are stated (DEL-03)
No acceptance by silence alone: Acceptance follows from silence alone (DEL-06)
Rejection and correction: Rejection is not addressed (DEL-07)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Are the service levels defined as named, measurable standards (for example availability, response time)? (2) Does each measure have a stated target? (3) Does the clause say how, and over what period, performance is measured? (4) Must performance against the service levels be reported to the other party? (5) Does the clause state a consequence for missing a service level (for example credits, a remedial plan, a right to terminate)? (6) [Balance] [Only where the clause states a remedy for missed service levels] Does the clause leave other remedies available, rather than making the stated remedy the only one? (7) [Only where the clause excludes events or periods from measurement] Are the exclusions listed specifically? (8) Does the clause state a consequence for repeated or serious failure beyond the usual remedy (for example a right to terminate)?
unacceptable_triggers: Service levels are measurable: Only general commitments are given (SLA-01)
Targets are stated: No measure has a target (SLA-02)
Remedy for missed targets: No consequence is stated (SLA-05)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause identify what support covers (for example services, systems, products)? (2) Are the times when support is available and the contact channels stated? (3) Are incidents classified by severity or priority, with criteria for each class? (4) Does the clause state response or resolution times by category? (5) Does the clause provide for escalation of incidents that are not resolved in time? (6) Does the clause say whether updates, patches and fixes are included? (7) Does the clause deal with planned maintenance (notice or timing)? (8) [Only where the clause excludes matters from support] Are the exclusions listed specifically?
unacceptable_triggers: Scope of support: No scope is stated (SUP-01)
Response and resolution times: No times are stated (SUP-04)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause set a process for requesting, assessing and approving changes? (2) Are changes effective only when agreed in writing by both parties? (3) Must a change request be assessed for its effect on price, timing and scope? (4) Does the clause state how quickly a change request must be answered? (5) [Balance] Can both parties request a change, and is neither forced to accept one without agreement? (6) Does the clause say how price and timetable adjustments from an approved change are recorded?
unacceptable_triggers: Change process is set: No process is stated (CHG-01)
Changes are not one-sided: One party may impose changes (CHG-05)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Are the fees stated or determinable (amounts, rates, or a specific reference to where they are set)? (2) Does the clause say how fees are calculated (for example fixed, time-based, usage-based)? (3) Does the clause say when and how invoices are issued? (4) Does the clause state when payment is due? (5) Does the clause say whether fees are fixed or how they may change? (6) [Balance] [Only where the clause lets one party change fees without the other's agreement] Is that change limited (by a cap, an index, notice or a right to object)? (7) Does the clause let the paying party dispute an invoice and say how the disputed amount is treated? (8) Does the clause state the consequence of late payment (for example interest or suspension)? (9) Does the clause say whether expenses are included or extra, and who approves or bears them? (10) [Balance] [Only where the clause lets a party suspend or stop work for non-payment] Is suspension conditional on written notice and a chance to pay first?
unacceptable_triggers: Fees are identified: No fees or basis are stated (FEE-01)
Payment timing: No payment timing is stated (FEE-04)
Fee changes are limited: The change is unrestricted (FEE-06)
Disputed invoices: No right to dispute is stated (FEE-07)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause require the receiving party to keep information confidential and limit how it is used? (2) Is confidential information identified by a definite description (categories, marking or a defined test)? (3) Does the clause state the level of care required to protect the information? (4) Does the clause list exceptions such as public information, information already known, independently developed or received from a third party? (5) Does the clause allow disclosure required by law or a regulator, with notice to the other party? (6) [Balance] Do the confidentiality duties apply to both parties in the same way? (7) Is the period for which the duty lasts stated? (8) Does the clause deal with return or destruction of confidential information on request or when the agreement ends? (9) [Balance] Is disclosure limited to people who need to know it and are bound by confidentiality?
unacceptable_triggers: Duty to keep information confidential: No duty is stated (CON-01)
Confidential information is described: Confidential information is not described (CON-02)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause require compliance with applicable data protection or privacy law? (2) Does the clause state each party's role for personal data (for example controller and processor, or an equivalent)? (3) [Balance] Is processing of personal data limited to stated purposes or documented instructions? (4) Does the clause describe what data and processing it covers (for example types of data, purpose, duration), directly or by reference? (5) Must a party notify the other of a personal data breach or security incident? (6) Must a party help with data subject requests or regulator enquiries? (7) Does the clause deal with moving personal data to another country or location? (8) Does the clause deal with return or deletion of personal data and other data when processing or the agreement ends? (9) [Only where the clause deals with security of data or systems] Does the clause set a security standard (a named framework or specified measures)? (10) [Only where the clause deals with security of data or systems] Does the clause identify specific controls (for example access control, encryption, logging)? (11) [Only where the clause deals with security of data or systems] Must the responsible party investigate, contain and report on incidents? (12) [Only where the clause deals with security of data or systems] Does the clause give a way to verify compliance (for example audit, certification, reports)? (13) [Only where the clause deals with security of data or systems] Is access to data limited to people who need it or who are bound by confidentiality?
unacceptable_triggers: Compliance with data protection law: No compliance duty is stated (DPP-01)
Processing is limited to purposes: No limit is stated (DPP-03)
Breach notification: No duty is stated (DPP-05)
Security standard is stated: No standard is stated (DPP-09)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause state who owns each kind of IP (pre-existing IP, newly created IP, data)? (2) [Balance] Does the clause say that each party keeps its pre-existing IP? (3) [Only where one party needs to use IP that the other party owns] Is a licence granted with its scope (purpose, duration, whether exclusive) stated? (4) [Only where the clause passes ownership of IP from one party to another] Is the transfer worded as an assignment that takes effect (not only a promise to assign later)? (5) [Balance] Does the clause state limits on how each party may use the other's IP (for example only for the agreed purpose)? (6) Does the clause deal with third-party claims that IP infringes their rights (responsibility or remedy, directly or by reference to an indemnity)?
unacceptable_triggers: Ownership is allocated: Ownership is not stated (IPR-01)
Licence where ownership stays: No licence is granted (IPR-03)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Do the parties state that they have authority to enter the agreement? (2) Is the standard for performing the services stated (for example skill and care, conformance to a specification)? (3) Do the parties warrant compliance with applicable laws? (4) Is there a warranty that the services or deliverables do not infringe others' rights? (5) Does the clause state the remedy for breach of warranty (for example correction, re-performance, refund)? (6) [Only where the clause gives performance or conformance warranties] Is the period during which the warranty applies stated? (7) [Balance] [Only where the clause disclaims warranties] Does the disclaimer leave the express warranties intact?
unacceptable_triggers: Performance standard: No standard is stated (REP-02)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause identify the matters that trigger the indemnity (for example third-party claims, IP infringement, breach of law)? (2) Is it clear which party indemnifies which? (3) Does the clause say what losses are covered (for example damages, costs, legal fees, settlements)? (4) [Balance] Are indemnities mutual or, if one-sided, limited to matters within the indemnifying party's control? (5) Does the clause set out how claims are handled (prompt notice, control of defence, cooperation)? (6) Does the clause say whether the indemnity is subject to the liability cap or exclusions? (7) [Balance] Must the indemnified party take reasonable steps to limit its loss?
unacceptable_triggers: Triggers are defined: No triggers are identified (IND-01)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause state clearly whether liability is limited and, if so, by what amount or formula? (2) [Balance] [Only where the clause limits liability] Does the limit apply to both parties, or are differences between them explained? (3) [Only where the clause excludes types of loss (for example indirect or consequential loss, loss of profit)] Are the excluded losses identified specifically and applied to both parties? (4) Does the clause leave unlimited the liabilities that cannot lawfully or fairly be limited (for example fraud, death or personal injury caused by negligence)? (5) Does the clause say whether the limit applies to data breach, confidentiality breach, IP infringement and indemnities? (6) Does the clause say whether the limit applies per claim, per period or in total?
unacceptable_triggers: The limit is clear: It is not stated, or the wording is contradictory (LOL-01)
The limit applies fairly: It protects one party only (LOL-02)
Liabilities that cannot be limited: None is addressed, or the clause limits them (LOL-04)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause name the types of insurance that must be held? (2) Does the clause say which party must hold each insurance? (3) Are minimum amounts of cover stated? (4) Must the insuring party show evidence of cover (for example a certificate) when asked or at set times? (5) Does the clause say how long cover must be kept (for example during the term and for a period after)? (6) Does the clause say whether insurance limits or otherwise affects a party's liability?
unacceptable_triggers: Required cover is identified: No insurance is required (INS-01)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause require compliance with applicable laws and regulations? (2) Does the clause identify the laws, codes or standards that must be followed? (3) [Only where the clause requires compliance with a party's policies or code of conduct] Are those policies identified or provided? (4) Does the clause address bribery and corruption? (5) Must a party tell the other if it breaches a law or policy that affects the agreement? (6) [Balance] [Only where the clause deals with changes in law] Does the clause say who bears the effort and cost of complying with a change in law?
unacceptable_triggers: Duty to comply with law: No duty is stated (CMP-01)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause give a right to audit or inspect? (2) Does the clause say what can be audited (for example premises, systems, records)? (3) Does the clause say how often audits can take place? (4) Does the clause say how much notice must be given before an audit? (5) Must relevant records be kept, with a retention period? (6) Must the audited party cooperate and give access to records and people? (7) Must the audited party correct findings? (8) [Balance] Does the clause say who bears the cost of an audit?
unacceptable_triggers: Audit right: No right is given (AUD-01)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause say whether subcontracting is allowed and on what conditions (for example consent or notice)? (2) Does the clause say that the contracting party remains responsible for its subcontractors? (3) Must subcontractors be bound by obligations equivalent to the main agreement (for example confidentiality, security, data protection)? (4) [Balance] Does the other party have a right to approve or object to subcontractors? (5) Is a list or record of subcontractors kept or shared? (6) [Only where the clause gives a right to object to a subcontractor] Does the clause say what happens if an objection is not resolved?
unacceptable_triggers: Permission and conditions: It is not addressed (SUB-01)
Responsibility is retained: This is not stated (SUB-02)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) [Balance] Does the clause deal with transfer of rights or obligations to others, with rules that apply to both parties? (2) [Only where the clause requires consent for a transfer] Is consent subject to a stated standard (for example 'not unreasonably withheld') and a response time? (3) Does the clause deal with transfers to affiliates or on a merger or sale of the business? (4) [Balance] Does the party that transfers remain responsible for its obligations unless released? (5) [Only where the clause allows a transfer without consent in some cases] Must the other party be told of the transfer?
unacceptable_triggers: Consent for assignment: It is not addressed (ASG-01)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause define force majeure events (a list or a defined test)? (2) [Balance] Does the clause exclude events a party could prevent or control (for example its own labour disputes, failure of its own suppliers)? (3) Must the affected party notify the other of the event? (4) Must the affected party take steps to limit the effect and resume performance? (5) Does the clause say what is excused (for example delay, but not payment of sums already due)? (6) Does the clause say what happens to payment during the event? (7) Does the clause give a way out if the event continues for a stated period (for example a right to terminate)? (8) Does the clause say whether continuity or recovery obligations still apply during the event? (9) [Only where the clause deals with business continuity or disaster recovery] Does the clause require a business continuity or disaster recovery plan? (10) [Only where the clause deals with business continuity or disaster recovery] Does the clause say what the plan must cover (for example services, systems, data, locations)? (11) [Only where the clause deals with business continuity or disaster recovery] Does the clause state recovery timeframes or objectives? (12) [Only where the clause deals with business continuity or disaster recovery] Must the plan be tested or reviewed, and how often? (13) [Only where the clause deals with business continuity or disaster recovery] Must the plan or test results be shared with the other party? (14) [Only where the clause deals with business continuity or disaster recovery] Must a party notify the other when the plan is invoked or a disruption occurs? (15) [Only where the clause deals with business continuity or disaster recovery] Must gaps found in tests or events be corrected?
unacceptable_triggers: Events are defined: No definition is given (FOR-01)
Long-running events: No way out is stated (FOR-07)
Plan is required: No plan is required (FOR-09)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause name the law that governs the agreement? (2) Does the clause say where disputes are decided (specific courts or arbitration)? (3) Does the clause avoid conflicting statements about law or forum (for example courts in one place and arbitration elsewhere with no explanation)? (4) [Only where disputes are to be decided by arbitration] Are the rules and the seat of arbitration stated? (5) Does the clause set steps before formal proceedings (for example negotiation, escalation, mediation) with timeframes? (6) [Balance] Does the clause bind both parties to the same forum, or, if one party can choose, is that choice limited? (7) Does the clause preserve the right to seek urgent court relief? (8) Must the parties keep performing while a dispute is resolved?
unacceptable_triggers: Governing law is named: No governing law is named (LAW-01)
Forum is identified: No forum is named (LAW-02)
No conflicting provisions: There is a conflict (LAW-03)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause state the required form of notice (for example in writing)? (2) Are addresses or contact details for notices stated or referenced for each party? (3) Are the permitted delivery methods listed (for example hand, courier, post, email)? (4) Does the clause say when a notice is treated as received? (5) Does the clause say how a party changes its notice details?

The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause state that the parties' relationship is that of independent contractors? (2) Does the clause state that no partnership, agency, joint venture or employment relationship is created? (3) Does the clause state that neither party can bind the other? (4) Does the clause state that each party is responsible for its own personnel's costs, taxes and benefits? (5) Does the clause say who controls the manner and means of performance?
unacceptable_triggers: Status is stated: This is not stated (IC-01)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause say which documents make up the whole agreement? (2) [Balance] [Only where the clause contains entire agreement or exclusion wording] Does that wording leave liability for fraud intact? (3) Does the clause say that earlier agreements and communications on the same subject are replaced? (4) [Balance] [Only where the clause excludes reliance on statements outside the agreement] Does the exclusion of reliance apply to both parties?

The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause identify the documents that form the agreement? (2) Does the clause state an order of priority between the documents? (3) Does the clause say how a conflict is resolved (for example the higher document prevails to the extent of the conflict)? (4) Does the clause prevent lower-ranking documents (for example a work order) from overriding higher-ranking ones without express words? (5) [Balance] Does the clause exclude other terms (for example standard terms, purchase orders, online terms) from the agreement?
unacceptable_triggers: Priority order is stated: No order is stated (PRE-02)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause say how the agreement can be amended? (2) [Balance] Is any right of one party to change the terms alone (including by updating referenced terms) absent or limited? (3) Does the clause say who may sign an amendment for each party? (4) Does the clause say the amendment process covers the whole agreement, including schedules and orders? (5) Does the clause say that oral agreements or conduct do not change the agreement?
unacceptable_triggers: No one-sided changes: A party may change terms alone without limit (AMD-02)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause say that delay or failure to enforce a right is not a waiver? (2) Is a waiver effective only if it is in writing and signed by the waiving party? (3) Does the clause say that waiving one breach or right does not waive others?

The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause say that a term found invalid does not affect the rest of the agreement? (2) Does the clause provide for replacing an invalid term with a valid one that has the closest effect? (3) Does the clause name the grounds (invalid, illegal, unenforceable)?

The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause state that neither party is the agent or representative of the other? (2) Does the clause state that neither party may make commitments in the other's name? (3) Does the clause exclude partnership, joint venture or employment? (4) [Balance] [Only where the clause allows one party to act for the other in some cases] Is that authority limited in scope and recorded in writing?
unacceptable_triggers: No agency is created: This is not stated (NAA-01)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause state whether the arrangement is exclusive or non-exclusive? (2) Does the clause state that each party may deal with third parties for similar services? (3) Does the clause say whether any minimum volume or spend is promised? (4) [Balance] [Only where the clause grants exclusivity to a party] Is the exclusivity limited by scope, territory or time?
unacceptable_triggers: Exclusivity position is stated: It is not stated (NEX-01)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause require compliance with export control and sanctions laws? (2) Does the clause name the regimes or lists that apply? (3) Does each party confirm it is not a sanctioned or restricted party? (4) [Balance] [Only where the clause lets a party suspend or end the agreement for export or sanctions reasons] Is that right limited to the affected activity and subject to notice? (5) Must a party give the information the other needs to meet export and sanctions rules?
unacceptable_triggers: Duty to comply: No duty is stated (EXP-01)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause say whether using a party's name, logo or trademarks needs that party's consent? (2) Must consent be in writing and given before use? (3) Does the clause identify the uses covered (for example announcements, client lists, marketing, case studies)? (4) [Balance] Do the restrictions apply to both parties? (5) Does the clause allow disclosures that law or regulation require?
unacceptable_triggers: Consent for use of name: Use is allowed without consent, or the matter is not addressed (PUB-01)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause state that injunctive or other equitable relief is available for breach? (2) [Balance] Is the right to equitable relief available to both parties? (3) [Balance] Does the clause say equitable relief is in addition to other remedies? (4) Does the clause identify which breaches can justify relief (for example confidentiality or IP)?
unacceptable_triggers: Relief is available: It is not stated (EQR-01)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause require the parties to avoid conflicts of interest? (2) Does the clause describe what counts as a conflict of interest? (3) Must a party disclose an actual or possible conflict? (4) Does the clause say what follows if a conflict arises (for example stop the activity or terminate)?
unacceptable_triggers: Duty to avoid conflicts: No duty is stated (COI-01)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause list the provisions that continue after expiry or termination? (2) Does the clause keep rights and liabilities that arose before termination? (3) [Only where the clause says some provisions continue] Is the period for which they continue stated? (4) [Balance] Does survival protect both parties' interests?
unacceptable_triggers: Surviving provisions are identified: It is not stated (SUR-01)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause allow the agreement to be signed in separate counterparts? (2) Does the clause say the counterparts together form one agreement? (3) Does the clause allow electronic signature and electronic delivery of signed copies? (4) Does the clause say when the agreement takes effect if counterparts are signed on different dates?
unacceptable_triggers: Counterparts are allowed: This is not stated (CTP-01)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause identify which obligations or dates time is of the essence for? (2) [Balance] Does the clause apply to both parties' obligations? (3) Does the clause say what follows if the time is missed? (4) [Balance] Does the clause allow more time where delay is caused by the other party or an excused event?
unacceptable_triggers: Time-critical obligations are identified: No obligation or date is identified (TOE-01)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does the clause say which party bears each tax it covers (for example sales or transaction tax and withholding)? (2) Does the clause state whether fees include taxes? (3) [Balance] [Only where the clause deals with withholding tax or gross-up] Are the treatment of withholding and the documents needed stated? (4) Must the parties provide tax invoices, exemption certificates or other documents? (5) Does the clause say each party bears taxes on its own income and personnel?
unacceptable_triggers: Responsibility for taxes: No allocation is stated (TAX-01)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does each right or duty the clause creates say who, what and when? (2) Does the clause avoid terms that belong in a specific clause type (for example liability, payment or termination)? (3) [Balance] Do the rights in the clause apply to both parties in the same way? (4) Does any duty in the clause have a consequence or a way to act on it if it is not followed? (5) [Only where the clause says it applies despite other terms] Does the clause name the terms it overrides? (6) [Only where the clause sets up governance, review or relationship-management arrangements] Does each party appoint a named person or role to manage the relationship? (7) [Only where the clause sets up governance, review or relationship-management arrangements] Does the clause say how often governance meetings or reviews take place? (8) [Only where the clause sets up governance, review or relationship-management arrangements] Does the clause require progress or performance reports, with their content or frequency stated? (9) [Only where the clause sets up governance, review or relationship-management arrangements] Does the clause set how unresolved issues are escalated (levels or steps)? (10) [Only where the clause sets up governance, review or relationship-management arrangements] Does the clause say what the representatives can decide, and that their decisions do not change the agreement unless formally agreed?
unacceptable_triggers: Rights and duties are definite: Most are vague (MSC-01)
Escalation route: No escalation route is stated (MSC-09)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) Does any restriction that continues after the agreement ends last no longer than 12 months? (2) Is the restricted activity defined by a specific technology, product, service or industry? (3) Does the clause state its geographic scope, and is the restriction enforceable under the governing law (for example, California law generally voids post-termination non-competes)? (4) [Balance] Does the clause leave the client free to engage other vendors, build or buy competing solutions, and operate in any market?
unacceptable_triggers: Duration is limited: It lasts more than 12 months after the agreement ends, or has no end date (NCP-01)
Client is not restricted: The client is restricted (NCP-04)

acceptable_standard: The clause should satisfy each of these checks. (1) [Balance] Does the restriction bind both parties in the same way, rather than restricting the client alone? (2) Does the restriction end no later than 12 months after the agreement ends? (3) Is the restriction limited to personnel directly involved in the services? (4) Are general job advertisements not aimed at the other party's staff, and people who apply on their own initiative, excluded? (5) [Balance] [Only where the clause sets a fee or damages for hiring the other party's personnel] Is any such fee no more than 25% of the person's annual base salary?
unacceptable_triggers: Restriction is even-handed: Only the client is restricted (NSO-01)
